request: how do you find the median of an even number of values?

beats.intent: Six values 2, 4, 7, 9, 12, 15 marked on a number line
beats.narration: Six values, in order: two, four, seven, nine, twelve, fifteen.
beats.code:
stage.title("The median")
nl = draw_number_line(stage, x_range=(0, 16))
for v in (2, 4, 7, 9, 12, 15):
    mark_point(stage, nl, v)

beats.intent: The two middle values 7 and 9 lit
beats.narration: With six values there is no single middle: the middle two are seven and nine.
beats.code:
a = mark_point(stage, nl, 7, color=RED, label="7")
b = mark_point(stage, nl, 9, color=RED, label="9")

beats.intent: The point 8 halfway between them marked as the median
beats.narration: The median is halfway between them: eight.
beats.code:
m = mark_point(stage, nl, 8, color=GREEN, label="median 8", direction=DOWN)
stage.equation(r"\frac{7 + 9}{2} = 8")

request: what is the mode of a data set?

beats.intent: Bars of how many students chose each favourite colour: red 4, blue 7, green 3, yellow 5
beats.narration: Twenty students name their favourite colour.
beats.code:
stage.title("The mode")
bars = draw_bars(stage, [4, 7, 3, 5], labels=["red", "blue", "green", "yellow"])

beats.intent: The tallest bar, blue with 7, lit
beats.narration: The most common answer is blue, with seven votes: that is the mode.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, bars[1])
stage.caption("The mode is the most common value: blue")

request: what is the chance of drawing two aces from a deck?

beats.intent: A bar of 52 cards with 4 aces lit
beats.narration: A deck has fifty two cards, four of them aces.
beats.code:
stage.title("Two aces in a row")
cards = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=0.18, height=0.9, color=RED if k < 4 else GREY, fill_opacity=0.8) for k in range(52)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.03).shift(UP)
stage.play(FadeIn(cards))
stage.add(cards)
stage.caption("First card: 4 aces out of 52")

beats.intent: One ace removed, leaving 51 cards with 3 aces lit
beats.narration: If the first is an ace, three aces remain among fifty one cards.
beats.code:
stage.play(cards[0].animate.shift(DOWN * 2).set_opacity(0.3))
stage.caption("Second card: 3 aces out of 51")

beats.intent: The cards beside P = 4/52 × 3/51 = 1/221
beats.narration: Multiply: four fifty-seconds times three fifty-firsts is one in two hundred and twenty one.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\frac{4}{52} \times \frac{3}{51} = \frac{1}{221}")

request: two friends arrive at random within an hour and wait 15 minutes: do they meet?

beats.intent: A 60 by 60 square of arrival times, Ann across and Ben up
beats.narration: Plot Ann's arrival time across and Ben's up: every point in the square is one possible pair of times.
beats.code:
stage.title("Will they meet?")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 60), y_range=(0, 60), labels=("Ann", "Ben"))
sq = Polygon(ax.c2p(0, 0), ax.c2p(60, 0), ax.c2p(60, 60), ax.c2p(0, 60), color=GREY, fill_opacity=0.1)
stage.play(FadeIn(sq))
stage.add(sq)

beats.intent: The band where the times differ by at most 15 minutes shaded along the diagonal
beats.narration: They meet if their times are within fifteen minutes: a band along the diagonal.
beats.code:
band = Polygon(ax.c2p(0, 0), ax.c2p(15, 0), ax.c2p(60, 45), ax.c2p(60, 60), ax.c2p(45, 60), ax.c2p(0, 15), color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5)
stage.play(FadeIn(band))
stage.add(band)

beats.intent: The band beside P = 1 - (45/60)^2 = 7/16
beats.narration: The two corners left over are triangles of side forty five. The band is one minus three quarters squared: seven sixteenths.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"P = 1 - \left(\tfrac{45}{60}\right)^2 = \tfrac{7}{16}")

request: why is the derivative of x^3 equal to 3x^2?

beats.intent: Axes with y = x^3 from -2 to 2
beats.narration: Here is x cubed.
beats.code:
stage.title("The power rule")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(-2, 2), y_range=(-8, 8))
f = lambda x: x ** 3
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, f, color=BLUE, label="x^3")

beats.intent: A tangent sliding along the curve, flat at 0 and steep at the ends
beats.narration: Slide a tangent: flat at zero, steep at both ends.
beats.code: slide_tangent(stage, ax, f, -1.8, 1.8)

beats.intent: The slope curve 3x^2 drawn through the tangent slopes, with (1, 3) marked
beats.narration: Plot the slope at every point and you get three x squared: at one, the slope is three.
beats.code:
d = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: 3 * x ** 2, x_range=(-1.6, 1.6), color=YELLOW, label="3x^2")
p = mark_point(stage, ax, 1, 3, color=RED, label="slope 3 at x = 1")
stage.equation(r"\frac{d}{dx}x^3 = 3x^2")

request: if you drive there at 30 km/h and back at 60, what's your average speed?

beats.intent: Two bars for the time each way of a 60 km trip: 2 hours out, 1 hour back
beats.narration: Sixty kilometres each way. Out at thirty takes two hours; back at sixty takes one.
beats.code:
stage.title("Average speed")
bars = draw_bars(stage, [2, 1], labels=["out", "back"])
stage.caption("Hours for each 60 km leg")

beats.intent: The total of 120 km over 3 hours
beats.narration: In all you drive a hundred and twenty kilometres in three hours.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\frac{120\ \text{km}}{3\ \text{h}} = 40\ \text{km/h}")

beats.intent: A number line with 40 marked below 45, the naive average
beats.narration: That is forty, not forty five: you spend longer at the slow speed, so it counts for more.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
nl = draw_number_line(stage, x_range=(25, 65))
t = mark_point(stage, nl, 40, color=GREEN, label="true 40")
n = mark_point(stage, nl, 45, color=RED, label="naive 45", direction=DOWN)

request: which is cheaper: 3 for £2 or 5 for £3?

beats.intent: Two groups of items: 3 apples for £2 and 5 apples for £3
beats.narration: One shop sells three apples for two pounds, another five for three pounds.
beats.code:
stage.title("Best value")
a = draw_dots(stage, n=3, cols=3, where="left", color=RED)
b = draw_dots(stage, n=5, cols=5, where="right", color=GREEN)
stage.label(a, "3 for £2", direction=DOWN, color=RED)
stage.label(b, "5 for £3", direction=DOWN, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: Bars of the price per apple: 67p and 60p
beats.narration: Divide the price by the number: sixty seven pence each against sixty pence each.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
bars = draw_bars(stage, [0.667, 0.6], labels=["3 for £2", "5 for £3"])
highlight(stage, bars[1], color=GREEN)
stage.caption("5 for £3 is cheaper per apple")

request: how do you share 20 sweets in the ratio 2:3?

beats.intent: Twenty dots in a grid
beats.narration: Twenty sweets to share in the ratio two to three.
beats.code:
stage.title("Sharing in a ratio")
dots = draw_dots(stage, n=20, cols=5)

beats.intent: The dots coloured in 5 parts of 4 sweets each
beats.narration: Two plus three is five parts. Twenty sweets in five parts is four sweets a part.
beats.code:
shades = [RED, ORANGE, YELLOW, TEAL, PURPLE]
stage.play(*[dots[k].animate.set_color(shades[k // 4]) for k in range(20)])
stage.caption("5 parts of 4 sweets")

beats.intent: 2 parts coloured blue (8 sweets) and 3 parts green (12 sweets)
beats.narration: Two parts is eight sweets; three parts is twelve.
beats.code:
stage.play(*[dots[k].animate.set_color(BLUE) for k in range(8)], *[dots[k].animate.set_color(GREEN) for k in range(8, 20)])
stage.equation(r"20 \div 5 = 4", r"2 \times 4 = 8,\; 3 \times 4 = 12")

request: how can you measure a tree's height with an angle?

beats.intent: A right triangle: 20 m along the ground to the tree, the tree as the vertical side
beats.narration: Stand twenty metres from a tree.
beats.code:
stage.title("Height from an angle")
A, B, C = (-3, -1.5), (2, -1.5), (2, 1.5)
tri = draw_polygon(stage, [A, B, C], where=None)
ground = draw_line(stage, A, B, color=GREEN)
stage.label(ground, "20 m", direction=DOWN, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: The angle of 31 degrees at the observer looking up to the treetop
beats.narration: Look up to the top of the tree: the angle of elevation is thirty one degrees.
beats.code:
ang = Angle(Line(np.array([*A, 0]), np.array([*B, 0])), Line(np.array([*A, 0]), np.array([*C, 0])), radius=0.8, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(ang))
stage.add(ang)
stage.label(ang, "31°", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The tree side labelled h beside h = 20 tan 31° ≈ 12 m
beats.narration: Opposite over adjacent is the tangent, so the height is twenty times tan thirty one: about twelve metres.
beats.code:
tree = draw_line(stage, B, C, color=RED)
stage.label(tree, "h", direction=RIGHT, color=RED)
stage.equation(r"h = 20 \tan 31^\circ \approx 12\ \text{m}")

request: how much of a circle does the biggest square inside it cover?

beats.intent: A circle of radius 1
beats.narration: A circle of radius one has area pi.
beats.code:
stage.title("Square in a circle")
c = draw_circle(stage, radius=2)

beats.intent: A square inscribed with its corners on the circle and its diagonal as a diameter
beats.narration: The biggest square inside has its diagonal across the circle: a diameter, two.
beats.code:
sq = Square(side_length=2 * np.sqrt(2), color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.4).rotate(PI / 4).move_to(c.get_center())
sq.rotate(-PI / 4)
stage.play(Create(sq))
stage.add(sq)
diag = draw_line(stage, c.get_center() + np.array([-np.sqrt(2), -np.sqrt(2), 0]), c.get_center() + np.array([np.sqrt(2), np.sqrt(2), 0]), color=RED)

beats.intent: The shapes beside square area 2 against circle area π: 2/π ≈ 64%
beats.narration: A square with diagonal two has area two, so it covers two over pi of the circle: about sixty four percent.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\frac{2}{\pi} \approx 0.64")
